task_objective: Make Dataset Catalog context-menu actions operate on every selected dataset while retaining SelectItems selection behaviour.
tests_added: tests/test_catalog_service.py: five remove_many tests for matching removal, one notification, unknown IDs, an empty iterable, and survivor order.

tests/test_catalog_dock.py: 13 tests for de-duplicated row enumeration, batch remove/refresh/copy/insert behaviour, view-row ordering, and Rename/Reveal enablement and fan-out gates. The file grew from 24 to 37 tests.
design_decisions: CatalogService.remove_many materialises IDs once, filters and assigns the catalog once, and notifies once. Looping remove would write the full persisted catalog once per dataset.
CatalogDock enumerates sorted selectedIndexes rows. selectedRows is unusable with SelectItems because an ordinary cell selection does not select every column in its row.
Rename Alias is disabled for a multi-row selection rather than silently acting on the anchored entry. Batch rename needs an explicit future design.
Reveal in File Manager is enabled only when the selected datasets share one parent folder. It opens one folder, not one window per dataset.
SelectItems remains in place. This keeps the prior cell-selection behaviour and limits this change to batch action semantics.
Linux reveal_command now accepts a directory target directly. Without this adjustment, passing the shared folder to the existing Linux branch would open that folder's parent.

The pre-existing tests for clicked-cell anchoring, vertical-header row selection, context-menu copy/remove, and blank-space action disabling passed unchanged in the final suite.

deferred_or_unverified: On-screen confirmation is deferred. Offscreen tests prove enumeration, clipboard content, signals, action states, and one Popen call, but not visual disabled styling or an actual file-manager window. In a windowed session, run ./run.sh uv run wherewolf-desktop, Ctrl-click several datasets, then check the menu and actions.
Schema refresh still starts one worker per selected dataset. This existing fan-out is unchanged and uncapped; worker limiting is a separate plan.
SelectItems remains cell-based even though actions are row-based. Change it to SelectRows only in a focused follow-up if the visual affordance proves confusing.
Batch Remove has no undo. It unregisters datasets only and does not delete files, but re-adding several datasets remains manual.
Reveal behaviour for future non-local sources is unspecified and untested.
